claims_left_unchecked: the per-structure label quality, which is an algorithm's segmentation of clinical CT and was never going to be checkable from metadata

what_it_would_actually_contribute: ONE female-specific structure: 'breast', as a single undifferentiated soft-tissue label. Not left and right, and no mammary gland, nipple, areola, lobule or lactiferous duct. The body currently has none of these in EITHER sex, so this closes the envelope and none of the internal structure. AND IT IS NOT IN THE DATASET: the Zenodo archive holds the 117 total-task labels only. A breast label has to be PRODUCED by running the Apache-2.0 breasts subtask model on a female CT from the archive, so the breast is that model's drawing of that subject.
NOTHING toward female internal or external genitalia. The class map has no uterus, ovary, vagina or cervix, so the uterine.* and placental.* field groups stay at 0 supporting entities.
Sex-neutral organ geometry from female subjects, which is a different and weaker claim than female-specific anatomy: a liver from a female donor is a liver.
A prostate, which this body already has.
integration_cost_before_it_is_usable: Label volumes are NIfTI, not meshes; marching cubes then decimation then a watertightness gate.

Registration into this body is the problem that has already failed once here for skin: neither existing skin map encloses the bones (0.273 and 0.445 of bone vertices inside their own skin). Another subject's organ needs per-segment transformation and a known-answer containment test, not a self-computed residual.

A segmentation of a clinical CT is not a curated anatomical atlas. Any assembled body would be composited from subjects who are not each other and are not the Rajagopal subject the skeleton is scaled from, and must say so.
limitations: The tool is a segmentation model, so what it yields is one subject's organ boundaries as an algorithm drew them, carrying that algorithm's error. A card written against it must name the CT subject, not the model.
